cited_numbers.sentence: **PRECIS-2**, Pragmatic Explanatory Continuum Indicator Summary 2, rates how closely a trial reflects usual care.
**Sample.** The benchmark included 112 pediatric surgery systematic reviews for PRISMA and AMSTAR and 56 randomized PragMeta trials for PRECIS-2 (Section 2.1, p. 2).
Analysis counts varied by model and tool, and the second human's PRISMA and AMSTAR ratings were missing for 15 reviews (Table 2, p. 5).
Report Cohen's kappa, where 0 means chance agreement and 1 means perfect agreement (Section 2.3.1, p. 3).
Pool PRECIS-2 scores 1 and 2, and scores 4 and 5.
On PRISMA, individual models matched human consensus on 63% to 70% of ratings, compared with 89% for human rater 1 (Table 2, p. 5).
PRISMA kappa ranged from 0.40 to 0.51 for models, compared with 0.81 for the human rater (Table 2, p. 5).
On AMSTAR, individual models matched human consensus on 53% to 74% of ratings, compared with 89% for human rater 1 (Table 2, p. 5).
AMSTAR kappa ranged from 0.27 to 0.56 for models, compared with 0.80 for the human rater (Table 2, p. 5).
On PRECIS-2, individual models matched human consensus on 38% to 55% of ratings, compared with 75% for human rater 1 (Table 2, p. 5).
Weighted PRECIS-2 kappa ranged from 0.01 to 0.12 for models, compared with 0.57 for the human rater (Table 2, p. 5).
Across PRISMA, AMSTAR, and PRECIS-2, it averaged 63% agreement with human consensus, compared with 57% to 59% for the other models (Section 3.1.2, p. 6).
Its average kappa across the same tools was 0.40, compared with 0.24 to 0.31 for the other models (Section 3.1.2, p. 7).
On PRISMA, requiring 9 rather than 5 of 9 assessments to agree raised retained agreement with human consensus from 75% to 88% (Table 3, p. 7).
PRISMA kappa rose from 0.59 to 0.77, while deferral rose from 4% to 74% (Table 3, p. 7).
On AMSTAR, requiring 9 rather than 5 of 9 assessments to agree raised retained agreement with human consensus from 74% to 89% (Table 3, p. 7).
AMSTAR kappa rose from 0.56 to 0.82, while deferral rose from 6% to 84% (Table 3, p. 7).
On PRECIS-2, requiring 9 rather than 5 of 9 assessments to agree raised retained agreement with human consensus from 64% to 79% (Table 3, p. 7).
Weighted PRECIS-2 kappa rose from 0.11 to 0.49, while deferral rose from 18% to 88% (Table 3, p. 7).
The text gives 29% as the lower deferral figure (Section 3.1.3, p. 7).
On retained PRISMA ratings, rater 1 with Claude-2 matched consensus 96% of the time, compared with 89% with GPT-4 (Table 3, p. 7).
These pairs deferred 35% and 25% of PRISMA ratings, respectively (Table 3, p. 7).
The authors reported that 8 of 10 pairs had higher PRISMA agreement with consensus on retained ratings than the corresponding human alone (Section 3.1.4, p. 8).
On retained AMSTAR ratings, rater 1 matched consensus at 91% with GPT-4, 95% with Claude-3-Opus, and 96% with GPT-3.5 (Table 3, p. 7).
The pairs deferred 27%, 30%, and 52% of AMSTAR ratings, respectively (Table 3, p. 7).
The authors reported that 8 of 10 pairs had higher AMSTAR agreement with consensus on retained ratings than the corresponding human alone (Section 3.1.4, p. 8).
On PRECIS-2, rater 1 with GPT-3.5 matched consensus on 86% of retained ratings, versus 75% for rater 1 alone across all ratings (Tables 2 and 3, pp. 5 and 7).
The pair deferred 71% of its PRECIS-2 ratings (Table 3, p. 7).
Only rater 2 with GPT-3.5 significantly outperformed the same rater alone on PRECIS-2 agreement with consensus (Section 3.1.4, p. 8).
Human rater 1 matched consensus on 89% of PRISMA reporting ratings and 89% of AMSTAR methods ratings (Table 2, p. 5).
The same rater matched consensus on 75% of PRECIS-2 trial pragmatism ratings (Table 2, p. 5).
They agreed with each other on 91% of PRISMA reporting ratings and 88% of AMSTAR methods ratings (Table 2, p. 5).
Their agreement on PRECIS-2 trial pragmatism was 57% (Table 2, p. 5).
Across repeat runs of the same model, agreement ranged from 67% to 94% on PRISMA reporting and 64% to 94% on AMSTAR methods (Table 2, p. 5).
Repeat agreement on PRECIS-2 trial pragmatism ranged from 61% to 78% (Table 2, p. 5).
Median model cost per research report ranged from $0.012 for Mixtral-8x22B to $1.15 for GPT-4 (Table 1, p. 3).
GPT-3.5 took about 10 seconds per report, compared with about 2 minutes for GPT-4 (Table 1, p. 3).
Claude-2 processed all reports, but Claude-3-Opus and GPT-4 each missed 3 of 112 reviews for PRISMA and AMSTAR (Section 3.3, p. 8).
GPT-3.5 missed 3 of 112 reviews for PRISMA and 2 of 56 trials for PRECIS-2 (Section 3.3, p. 8).
Mixtral-8x22B missed 1 of 112 reviews for PRISMA and AMSTAR, and some models needed retries on up to 13% of reports (Section 3.3, p. 8).
The median per report was 14 passages for PRISMA reporting, 7 for AMSTAR methods, and 10 for PRECIS-2 trial pragmatism (Section 3.3, p. 8).
Quoted passages had 99% median text similarity to the original, but some models quoted the briefing instead of the report (Section 3.3, p. 8).
[[V-V3]] **Older checklist versions.** The benchmark did not use PRISMA 2020 or AMSTAR-2.
